question: How do intrinsic cation-site vacancies influence phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity in Cu2SnSe4?
answer: Intrinsic cation-site vacancies in Cu₂SnSe₄ significantly enhance phonon scattering, reducing lattice thermal conductivity to 0.6 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. The 1/4 vacant cation sites create strong phonon scattering centers, lowering thermal conductivity more effectively than vacancy-free analogues. This intrinsic vacancy-driven mechanism enables a peak thermoelectric figure of merit (zT) of ~0.6 without extrinsic modifications, demonstrating that naturally occurring vacancies can serve as a design strategy for high-performance thermoelectrics. Further optimization through band engineering could improve performance further.

The findings emphasize the role of intrinsic vacancies as a design strategy for discovering new thermoelectric materials.
